description: Small sap-sucking insects affecting many crops and ornamental plants. Rapid reproduction via telescoping generations allows populations to multiply quickly. Some species alternate between host plants; others are generalists. They produce honeydew, which leads to sooty mold growth. Aphids act as vectors for plant viruses.
life_cycle: Asexual reproduction dominates; females give live birth to female nymphs
Winged females disperse to new plants later in the season
In temperate regions, sexual reproduction occurs in autumn, overwintering as eggs
Symbiosis with Buchnera aphidicola provides essential amino acids
hosts: Vegetables, fruits, cereals, legumes, ornamental plants
symptoms_and_damage: Honeydew deposits on leaves and stems
favorable_conditions: Dense plant canopy and stressed plants
natural_enemies: Ladybird beetles (e.g., Coccinella septempunctata, Adalia bipunctata)
Entomopathogenic fungi (Neozygites fresenii, Beauveria bassiana, Metarhizium anisopliae, Lecanicillium lecanii)
biological_control: Release of predatory insects and parasitoids
Encourage natural enemies in gardens or greenhouses
Use of fungal biopesticides (Beauveria, Lecanicillium, Metarhizium)
chemical_control: Insecticides are often limited due to resistance (carbamates, organophosphates, pyrethroids)
Systemic insecticides may not penetrate flowers
For small infestations: insecticidal soap, strong water jets (contact action only)
prevention: Monitor populations using yellow-pan or Moericke traps
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization to reduce aphid attraction
Encourage mutualistic ants only in controlled environments
Crop rotation and maintaining plant health
ant_mutualism: Some ants farm aphids for honeydew, protect them from predators
Ants may carry aphid eggs over winter and return them to plants in spring
Ant attendance increases honeydew production and affects aphid behavior
adaptations: Woolly or fluffy wax coating for protection
Soldier morphs in gall-forming species for defense
Chemical defenses via cornicles (allomones, sticky wax, pheromones)
Ability to drop off plants to escape predators
